# `bin/close-run`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/close-run`](../../../bin/close-run)

## What it says about itself

```text
bin/close-run RUN [--no-mutate] [--timeout SEC]

RULES.md steps 2–4 in one command, plus the two lines the orchestrator would otherwise
compose by hand (LESSONS.md "`bin/close-run` performs steps 2 and 4", 2026-09-16). Never launches anything, never appends to
CLAIMS.md. In order:
  1. bin/verify-data                    (hash guard; a finding stops here)
  2. bin/check RUN --mutate             (artifacts + declared mutation tests; --no-mutate to skip)
  3. bin/merge RUN                      (verdict table)
  4. prints: verdict table path; result.md line count and prose flags; a MODEL: line for the run and for each
     referee run not answered by the one model its approval named; per claim its earned tag and its model-family
     line; a PROVED claim with only one of the two questions (reported, not refused); for every claimed PROVED
     claim without a live `holds` referee, the exact `bin/new-run … --role referee --claim RUN ID` lines (certify
     and hypotheses); for every VERIFIED / NUMERIC claim without a live `sentence` hold, its `--question sentence`
     line; for every claim missing only the cross-family read, the run to create, launched on a model of the other
     family (LESSONS.md "A cross-family certify read"); existing CLAIMS.md notes on any id this run supersedes; and the exact
     `bin/approve --ledger RUN ID…` (the user's) and `bin/ledger-claims RUN ID…` lines for the ids
     whose earned tag is recordable (not FALSIFIED / BLOCKED / PENDING); the second refuses without the first;
     and, for any id a claim supersedes, the live entries that depend on it (bin/claim-deps).
Exit 0 when check passed and nothing is pending; 1 otherwise (the printout says what).
```
